title: Free solutions without finite boards
claim: For a shift of finite type X on the tree of F2 over a finite alphabet (every finitary value law, after recoding): (1) a finite board exists iff the balance equations over X's tree patterns have a nonzero nonnegative solution (known: Piantadosi 2008, Theorem 3.6; Hellouin de Menibus and Maturana Cornejo, arXiv 1904.03907), and by Farkas' lemma there is none iff a potential on edge values makes every tree pattern gain; (2) Lemma A'': infinitely many pairwise disjoint non-rigid half-trees in one solution give a solution with trivial stabilizer; (3) L1, a doubly recurrent branching type, and (4) L2, Busemann functions mod 3 for a level law allowing (1, 0, 3), or their negatives for (3, 0, 1), each give such a solution; (5) Theorem W: every infinite X has a solution with trivial stabilizer (Case I by Lemma A''; Case II because the non-rigid ends of all solutions form a closed invariant set, hence the whole boundary, which contains an end fixed by no nontrivial element). So under Leibniz's rule the tree is a board exactly when a law has infinitely many solutions, none forces the plane, with Piantadosi's weakly periodic points no law forces one infinite board, and every infinite X is uncountable; the proof holds for F_n, n >= 2. (6, found after the census, not pre-registered) A level law on Z/3 with solutions has no finite board iff its tree patterns all drift up (more neighbours one level up than down) or all drift down. Checks (check.py, all passed): mirror invariance of the census, the 10 undecided laws settled by the mirrored horofunction, every balance verdict re-decided exactly (96 potentials, 32,604 explicit boards, 4 boards with potentials), small boards to 4 places consistent, and the 96 weakly aperiodic laws exactly the 48 + 48 drifting ones.
failure_conditions: A weakly aperiodic law with no solution of trivial stabilizer (against W).
A law certified by L1 or L2 whose solutions all have nontrivial stabilizers (against the certificates).
foundation_claim_scope: Boards made of identity distinctions on the names of the free group on two letters, under Leibniz's rule in full; finitary value laws over finite alphabets. Identity distinctions are distinctions of the law, never contact (A51).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the owner's go-ahead on 2026-11-10; read before publication by an independent referee (a fresh Claude agent given only the proof), which found no error and asked for the wording changes made.
validation.status: proved by hand; finite checks in check.py passed (result.json); target 6 added after the census and disclosed as post hoc
validation.novelty: Theorem W not found stated (bounded searches 2026-11-10: Piantadosi's 2008 paper and thesis, Cohen 2017, Bitar arXiv 2406.04132, Carroll and Penland, and the referee's searches); the argument is short and uses standard tools (Baire, Konig, the minimal boundary action), so folklore risk is moderate. Target 1 is known (Piantadosi 2008, Theorem 3.6; the Chazottes-Gambaudo-Gautero condition, Hellouin de Menibus and Maturana Cornejo arXiv 1904.03907). Targets 2 to 4 and 6 are elementary.
